text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128,256],"swizzle":[0]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1},"rationale":"Initial plan. M=N=K=2048 is divisible by all chosen tiles. block_M in {32,64,128}, block_N in {64,128,256}, block_K in {32,64}, stages 1-3, threads 128/256 give a compact but non-trivial search under the 32KB portability cap. Shared estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N) is checked by HiGHS against the limit. Swizzle fixed to [0] for a row-major baseline per instructions; serpentine panels deferred until feedback. Threads 128 and 256 included as a cheap early hypothesis on warp layout; block_N=256 probes wider-N alternatives and stage=3 approaches stage=4 without inflating footprint beyond cap for small tiles. Objective is equal weighting of traffic, launches, pipeline, footprint; will revise after simulator feedback on whether panel reuse or thread changes affect latency. Validation scope: Metal numerical checks execute exact source/TIR; CUDA binaries are not run; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements."}
